title: Lexicon
description: A language's lexicon (lexicons/<lang>/lexemes.yaml; ADR 0145): every lexeme, in one list sorted by id. It is flat (the owner, 2026-11-20): no entry says which unit of which course teaches it. Courses point at it.

provenance.description: For every entry that gives none of its own.

Lexeme.title: Lexeme
Lexeme.description: One lexeme. What kind it is shows in what it has: a part of speech (casa, tener); `realises`, a value head, a feature value with a meaning (PAST, uz -ga); `head`, a function head (AGENT, a participle's pattern). An entry has one of the three. A lexeme that merges onto a base (ADR 0158) may say what it merges onto (`on`), what the word then requires (`requires`) and which stem it makes the base take (`selects`: a stem id, several, the first the base has a template for, or a pattern's templates; of several lexemes that select, the last in the token wins: apc's perfect takes the perfect stem, its 1sg ending the short one).

pos.description: Its one part of speech, a UD tag.

realises.description: The dimension value it is (ADR 0145: a value head): {Case: Dat}.

on.description: What it merges onto (ADR 0158): the part of speech of the word's base, and what the word must already have from the lexemes merged before it, nearer its base (es -o on a finite indicative present verb). Merging runs outward from the base, so these say the order: a lexeme merged where its `on` does not hold is an error.

needs.description: Features the word must have some value for already, whatever the value (arb's mood after the number ending: needs Number).

complete.description: Merges only onto a complete word: one whose every requirement is met (arb's pronoun suffixes onto ʾaktubu, never onto ʾaktub-; a proclitic onto a whole word).

at.description: Which side of its base it stands (a prefix or proclitic before, a suffix, ending or zero morpheme after): merged on the other side it is an error.

requires.description: The features a word it is merged into must then have, brought by other lexemes (ADR 0158: finite-ness requires person and tense). A word is complete, and written, once every requirement its category and its lexemes raise is met.

feats.description: Its lexical features. What Universal Dependencies says of the word (PronType: Dem, NumType: Card), and a feature its language declares lexical for its category only where no default gives it: mano {Gender: Fem}. Each of the second kind is a part to learn (ADR 0146).

chooses.description: Features its language declares lexical for its category that this lexeme's tokens choose instead: hermano, whose tokens are masculine or feminine. By ADR 0145 a noun's feminine is a derivative, and a lexeme of its own where it is listed; until that is decided for a lexeme, the value stays on its tokens, and the entry says so here.

classes.description: The classes of its language it belongs to: tener [e-ie, go].

notes.description: Notes shown with it, by support language.

image.description: Its picture. In a lexicon the file is relative to the lexicon's own file.

citation.description: The feature values of the form its entry is spelled in (its lemma: what a word card shows), where they are not its category's `citation` (language.yaml): apc's 2a3ed (sitting), a verb the course teaches as its masculine singular participle, not as its he-past.

forms.description: The forms and stems no rule gives yet (ADR 0145): each listed or pinned.

allomorphs.description: Its forms by context, where it has several and no rule gives them (uz -ga, -ka after k, -qa after q).

base.description: A derivative's base lexeme, where something about the derivative is listed (ADR 0145: m3allem, from 3allam).

pattern.description: A derivative's function head (the agentive pattern).

spelled.description: Its spelling in an orthography, pinned where that orthography's projection is not written yet or does not give it (ADR 0148: a pinned spelling a projection cannot account for is a finding). The first is the one shown.

readings.description: Its reading in a scheme, pinned (ADR 0117) until the projection gives it.

FunctionHead.title: FunctionHead
FunctionHead.description: A function head's signature (ADR 0145): what it takes, what it makes, which features it sets.

LexicalForm.title: LexicalForm
LexicalForm.description: A lexeme's one lexical form (ADR 0145): in its own script, fully specified, every spelling and the phonemes projected from it. Its shape depends on the kind of lexeme: a string in the language's notation (docs/lexical-forms/<lang>.md); a base's radicals, Form and vowels; a pattern's templates; a listed item's parts; a logograph with what picks its reading.

RadicalForm.title: RadicalForm
RadicalForm.description: A Semitic base (ADR 0145): its radicals, stored (a hollow verb's middle one shows only in some forms); its Form or stem, as its language names them (apc I to X and Q; hbo qal, nifal); and the vowels its Form leaves open. The root class is never stored: it follows from the radicals.

vowels.description: By the slot its language names (apc: past, present).

source.description: Where its radicals, Form and vowels are from, for reviewers: a reference and page (kline 75), course (the course writes the form) or deduced.

basis.description: What a deduced radical or vowel was deduced from, for reviewers (never shown to a learner): every entry with one is on the review list.

note.description: What else a reviewer should know of it (never shown to a learner).

PatternForm.title: PatternForm
PatternForm.description: A pattern (ADR 0145, 0150): its own letters and vowels around numbered slots for a base's radicals, one template per root class.

ListedParts.title: ListedParts
ListedParts.description: A listed item whose form is its parts' (darse cuenta; writer, an author): only its meaning is listed. `inflects` names the part that takes the forms (me di cuenta).

Logograph.title: Logograph
Logograph.description: The one exception to a single tier (ADR 0145): a character cannot say its sound, so the form is the character with what picks its reading, in the notation of its tradition (lzh: its Qieyun position; yue: a reading only where the table gives several or a tone changes).

LexemeForm.title: LexemeForm
LexemeForm.description: A form or a stem of a lexeme that the language's written rules do not give, with the feature values it covers (ADR 0145: an irregular is stored once, with the features it covers; the most specific that fits wins). One of `form` and `stem`. With `before`, it holds only where the rest of its token holds that condition, as an allomorph's `before` (a stem before a suffixed pronoun: hbo אַחֶי- in אַחֶיךָ), and is then more specific than a form of the same values without it; it never holds of a lexeme realised alone (a paradigm's cell). With no `feats`, it is for a token that chooses no value, never for a cell: an uninflected word's form (a preposition's stem before a suffix, hbo לָ- in לָנוּ; free variants, הִנֵּנִי beside הִנְנִי).

form.description: The whole form, in the language's lexical-form notation (fue).

stem.description: A stem the regular endings go on (tuv).

status.description: listed: the language has no rule for it, so it is a part to learn; it needs its `statement`. pinned: a rule gives it and ours is not written yet; stored and checked, never counted, never a learner's part.

free.description: A free variant (ADR 0145): where another form of the lexeme is as specific for a cell, the two are no tie; both are accepted and the first is shown.

statement.description: Who says the language has no rule for it. A draft counts until it is signed off (the owner, round 6).

spelled.description: Its spelling in an orthography, pinned where that orthography's projection is not written yet or does not give it (ADR 0148: a pinned spelling a projection cannot account for is a finding). The first is the one shown.

readings.description: Its reading in a scheme, pinned (ADR 0117) until the projection gives it.

Allomorph.title: Allomorph
Allomorph.description: One form of a lexeme by context. With no condition it is the one used elsewhere, or one whose condition no one has stated yet. It has `form`, or the spellings pinned until its language has a lexical-form notation.

free.description: true: a form the language's writers use beside the one the conditions choose, where its own conditions hold (anywhere, with none): a scribe's other spelling of a suffix (chg's locative دا beside ده), or a form the course writes where no condition tells it from the other (hbo בַּ, the preposition with an article its tokens do not list). Never the one chosen: a token's realisation gives it as an alternative.

spelled.description: Its spelling in an orthography, pinned where that orthography's projection is not written yet or does not give it (ADR 0148: a pinned spelling a projection cannot account for is a finding). The first is the one shown.

readings.description: Its reading in a scheme, pinned (ADR 0117) until the projection gives it.

Scope.title: Scope
Scope.description: Where a lexeme or a form is said (ADR 0145): a range of varieties and a range of registers. Everywhere unless stated.
